key_insight: For welding property prediction, stacking ensemble learning achieved higher task-wise accuracy than a multitask neural network, while MTNN still demonstrated strong shared-task generalization.
engineering_relevance: The study helps engineers choose between a shared-model approach for related outputs and a high-accuracy ensemble when predicting UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness in welding processes.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers, task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning
Predicted three welding responses: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness
Evaluated performance using RMSE and R^2
evidence_signal: MTNN reported RMSE/R^2 of 0.1288/0.6724 for UTS, 0.0886/0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.1125/0.8407 for HAZ hardness, while stacking improved to 0.0263/0.9863, 0.0467/0.9782, and 0.1109/0.8453, respectively.
watch_item: Stacking ensembles can be more task-specific and computationally heavier, so they may be harder to deploy when simplicity, transfer across related tasks, or limited data are priorities.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
